accept_create_attribute.title: Create an attribute acceptance plan
accept_create_attribute.summary: Choose a sample size and acceptance number for pass/fail inspection of a lot.
accept_create_attribute.why: You need an inspection rule before sampling: inspect n items, then accept the lot if at most c sampled items are nonconforming. JASP designs a single-stage rule from quality levels and agreed risks.

availability.note: Stable module listed in the official catalogue on 29 October 2026. Menu and options checked against official tagged source; not executed in the desktop application.

setup.title: Enter the quality agreement
setup.text: Enter Lot size (N), Acceptable Quality Level (AQL), Rejectable Quality Level (RQL / LTPD), Producer's risk (α), and Consumer's risk (β). Enter proportions: 0.01 means 1%. AQL is the acceptable reference quality; RQL is the poor-quality reference. Require AQL < RQL.

setup.title: Choose the inspection model
setup.text: Use Binomial for independent pass/fail outcomes with an approximately constant nonconforming probability. Use Hypergeometric for sampling without replacement from a finite lot: enter N and ensure N multiplied by every quality level, including the plot grid, is an integer. Poisson is an available count model/rare-event approximation; keep the definition and exposure of a defect consistent.

setup.title: Inspect the proposed rule
setup.text: Select Summary table and OC curve. Read the generated n and c, and verify acceptance probabilities at AQL and RQL. AOQ curve and ATI curve assume rectification of rejected lots by full inspection and replacement of nonconforming items.

checks: No dataset is required. This analysis designs a rule; it does not inspect a lot or import observed pass/fail results.
Producer's risk is P(reject at AQL); consumer's risk is P(accept at RQL). Neither is a posterior probability that this particular lot is bad.
Count nonconforming items once in a pass/fail plan. Do not silently replace that count with the number of separate flaws on the items.
Agree the plan and random sampling procedure before inspection. A plan does not guarantee every accepted item conforms.
report: N, distribution, AQL, RQL, α, β, and the generated n and c.
The OC curve and actual achieved risks; any rectification assumptions.

example.title: Plan an incoming seal inspection
example.story: A synthetic planning exercise for a lot of 1,000 seals: 1% nonconforming is the acceptable reference; 6% is the rejectable reference.
instructions: Select Hypergeometric. Set the proportion range From 0, To 0.10, Step size 0.001.
Request Summary table and OC curve. Record JASP's n and c before collecting inspection results.

accept_analyze_attribute.title: Evaluate an attribute acceptance plan
accept_analyze_attribute.summary: Examine the risks and inspection effort of an existing single-stage or multistage rule.
accept_analyze_attribute.why: You already know the sample sizes and acceptance/rejection thresholds. JASP evaluates their operating characteristics and checks them against your quality agreement.

availability.note: Stable module listed in the official catalogue on 29 October 2026. Menu and options checked against official tagged source; not executed in the desktop application.

setup.title: Describe the existing rule
setup.text: For Single Sampling Plan, enter Lot size (N), Sample size (n), and Acceptance number (c); Rejection number (r) is c + 1. For Multiple Sampling Plan, enter Number of stages and each stage's n, c, and r. The n values are additional samples at each stage; c and r apply to cumulative nonconforming counts.

setup.title: Check performance
setup.text: Choose Binomial, Hypergeometric, or Poisson to match the sampling model. Enable Assess attribute plan, or Assess sampling plan in the multistage section, and enter AQL, RQL / LTPD, and the two risks. Select OC curve and Summary table; the ASN curve shows average sample number for multistage sampling.

setup.title: Separate evaluating a rule from using it
setup.text: This screen takes plan settings, not observed inspection rows. Apply an agreed single-stage rule manually: accept if observed nonconforming count d ≤ c, reject if d ≥ r. At an intermediate stage, continue when c < cumulative d < r. Do not change the plan after seeing d.

checks: Multistage acceptance/rejection numbers must be nondecreasing; the last r must equal the last c + 1. Total planned sample size cannot exceed the lot size.
Hypergeometric quality-grid values must correspond to whole numbers of nonconforming items in the lot.
AOQ and ATI require rejected-lot rectification. ASN describes sampling to a decision and does not include all rectification work.
Analyze Attribute Plan evaluates supplied multistage plans; Create Attribute Plan designs a single-stage plan.
report: All stage sizes and cumulative decision thresholds, sampling distribution, lot size, and intended risks.
Acceptance probabilities at AQL and RQL, OC curve, and ASN when comparing staged plans.

example.title: Compare one inspection with a two-stage rule
example.story: Synthetic candidate plans for 1,000 connectors illustrate how a staged rule can stop early. These settings are teaching candidates, not a certified inspection standard.
instructions: Single Sampling Plan: N = 1000, n = 100, c = 4; choose Binomial.
Multiple Sampling Plan: N = 1000; 2 stages; stage 1: n = 50, c = 1, r = 4; stage 2: n = 50, c = 4, r = 5.
Use AQL = 0.01, RQL = 0.10, α = 0.05, β = 0.10 to assess both; request OC curves and the multistage ASN curve.

If the first sample has 2 nonconforming connectors, the staged rule continues. If the second adds 2, the cumulative count is 4 and the rule accepts. This comparison is manual, not an output calculated from inspection rows in JASP.

accept_create_variable.title: Create a variable acceptance plan
accept_create_variable.summary: Design a sampling rule that uses continuous measurements and a critical distance k.
accept_create_variable.why: You measure a quality characteristic such as diameter or strength, and want to select n and k before inspecting a lot. The plan uses a normal-distribution model and distinguishes known from estimated standard deviation.

availability.note: Stable module listed in the official catalogue on 29 October 2026. Menu and options checked against official tagged source; not executed in the desktop application.

setup.title: Set the planning requirements
setup.text: Enter Lot size (N), AQL, RQL / LTPD, Producer's risk (α), and Consumer's risk (β). These quality levels are proportions nonconforming, not measurement limits such as 9.95 mm. The planning screen requires settings, not a measurement dataset.

setup.title: Choose how variability will be treated
setup.text: Select Standard Deviation (Historical) known only when a defensible external standard deviation will be used for lot decisions. Otherwise clear it: the unknown-SD plan uses variability estimated from the inspection sample. The choice changes n and k.

setup.title: Review and carry the plan forward
setup.text: Request Summary table and OC curve, and record the generated n and Critical Distance (k). Use Accept/Reject Lots to apply the selected rule to measurements and specification limits. AQL/RQL and α/β define the planning performance; LSL/USL define item conformance.

checks: The normal measurement model, independent random sampling, and the chosen treatment of SD must be credible. A few passing normality-test results do not establish these assumptions.

The planning screen has no specification-limit or two-sided-plan switch. Do not assume its OC curve proves a particular two-sided rule has the requested combined-tail risks; review that rule before operational use.
A historical SD should represent the same measurement process and conditions; estimating it from the very sample being inspected is an unknown-SD analysis.
AOQ and ATI curves assume rectification of rejected lots; use them only if that matches the inspection policy.
report: N, quality/risk requirements, known or unknown SD, generated n and k, and the OC curve.
The measurement model, specification scheme, and sampling/rectification assumptions.

example.title: Plan a strength inspection
example.story: A synthetic supplier qualification exercise uses tensile strength measurements and a prespecified lower strength limit.
instructions: Select Standard Deviation (Historical) known and request OC curve and Summary table.
Record n and k, then clear the known-SD option and compare the required plan. Do not substitute the known-SD k into an unknown-SD inspection.

accept_analyze_variable.title: Evaluate a variable acceptance plan
accept_analyze_variable.summary: Check the operating characteristics of an existing n-and-k inspection rule.
accept_analyze_variable.why: A contract, previous design, or candidate plan already specifies n and k. You need to assess its acceptance probabilities and check the planned producer and consumer protection.

availability.note: Stable module listed in the official catalogue on 29 October 2026. Menu and options checked against official tagged source; not executed in the desktop application.

setup.title: Enter the rule
setup.text: Enter Lot size (N), Sample size (n), and k. Set Standard deviation (historical) known to match the actual inspection rule. The same numerical n and k can have different operating characteristics when SD is estimated rather than known.

setup.title: Assess the required risks
setup.text: Enable Assess variable plan. Enter Acceptable Quality Level (AQL), Rejectable Quality Level (RQL / LTPD), Producer's risk (α), and Consumer's risk (β). Use proportions and keep AQL below RQL. Inspect the assessment table instead of presuming a familiar n and k meet the agreement.

setup.title: Examine the range of lot qualities
setup.text: Set the Proportion non-conforming items range; request Summary table and OC curve. Add AOQ curve or ATI curve only for a rectifying inspection policy. To decide about an observed lot, use Accept/Reject Lots with its measurements or summary statistics.

checks: This analysis assesses a single-stage normal-model plan. It takes no observed measurement column and makes no decision for a particular lot.
The quality proportion on the OC horizontal axis is different from a measurement specification limit.
The screen does not calibrate the combined risks of arbitrary two-sided specifications. Match the evaluated plan to the intended specification and decision rule.
Check random sampling and the justification for known SD; a favorable OC curve relies on its statistical model.
report: N, n, k, known/unknown SD, AQL, RQL, and target and achieved producer/consumer risks.
OC curve and any AOQ/ATI assumptions; the inspection rule selected before data collection.

example.title: Review a proposed 24-item measurement plan
example.story: Synthetic settings illustrate how the variability assumption affects a supplied inspection rule.
instructions: Enter N = 1000, n = 24, k = 1.309 and select Standard deviation (historical) known.
Enable Assess variable plan; enter AQL = 0.05, RQL = 0.15, α = 0.05, β = 0.10.
Request Summary table and OC curve. Then clear the known-SD option and inspect how the assessment changes.
Use Create Variable Plan to obtain a newly calibrated rule when the assumptions change.

accept_decide_variable.title: Accept or reject a lot from measurements
accept_decide_variable.summary: Apply a prespecified variable sampling rule to one lot using the k-method.
accept_decide_variable.why: You have inspected a random sample from one lot and already have the relevant n, k, specification limits, and SD assumption. JASP provides a lot decision from the measurements or their summary statistics.

availability.note: Stable module listed in the official catalogue on 29 October 2026. Menu and options checked against official tagged source; not executed in the desktop application.

setup.title: Supply one lot's evidence
setup.text: Assign one Scale column to Measurement. Each row is one sampled item from the lot. Alternatively leave Measurement empty and enter Sample size (n), Sample mean, and Sample standard deviation in Specify sample statistics directly (used if dataset is not available).

setup.title: Enter the agreed decision rule
setup.text: Enter k from the chosen plan. Select Lower Specification Limit (LSL), Upper Specification Limit (USL), or both, and enter the limits. Select Standard deviation (historical) and enter its value only for a known-SD rule; otherwise JASP uses sample SD.

setup.title: Read the decision in its context
setup.text: Inspect the sample statistics, standardized distance(s), and decision. For a one-sided rule, accept when the mean's distance from the limit, divided by the applicable SD, is at least k. Two-sided rules depend on the SD assumption and both tail areas; when both limits and historical SD are selected, enter AQL and RQL as requested.

setup.title: Colleague preview — 7 November 2026
setup.text: All 24 original measurements are preserved with Diameter_cm = Diameter_mm / 10. Use Measurement = Diameter_cm, LSL .995 cm, historical SD .004 cm, k=1.309 and USL off. Equivalent units avoid the inactive-upper-limit validation problem. Mean 1.002020833 cm; standardized lower distance 1.755208333 gives Accept under this illustrative prespecified rule. The raincloud displays the same 24 values.

columns.name: Diameter_mm
columns.description: One diameter per randomly sampled component from a single lot; assign to Measurement.

columns.name: Diameter_cm
columns.description: Original Diameter_mm divided by ten, in cm.

checks: Use the planned sample size. This screen applies the supplied k; it does not verify that the sample size and k satisfy your target risks.
Keep lots separate: there is no lot-grouping assignment box. Filter or prepare one lot at a time.
Check measurement quality, normal-model plausibility, and positive sample SD. Prespecify the rule and limits before seeing the sample.
Acceptance is a sampling-policy decision; it does not establish zero nonconforming items or process stability.

All 24 original measurements are preserved with Diameter_cm = Diameter_mm / 10. Use Measurement = Diameter_cm, LSL .995 cm, historical SD .004 cm, k=1.309 and USL off. Equivalent units avoid the inactive-upper-limit validation problem. Mean 1.002020833 cm; standardized lower distance 1.755208333 gives Accept under this illustrative prespecified rule. The raincloud displays the same 24 values.
report: Lot identity, actual n, mean, SD, historical SD if used, limits, and k.
The decision, sampling method, plan justification, and any departures from the inspection protocol.

example.title: Inspect a lot of machined shafts
example.story: Twenty-four synthetic diameter measurements from one lot demonstrate a lower-limit decision; the settings are for teaching.
instructions: Assign Diameter_cm; set k=1.309, LSL=.995 cm, historical SD=.004 cm, USL off.
Check mean 1.002020833 cm and standardized distance 1.755208333; Accept follows only the specified illustrative rule.

accept_bayesian_single.title: Bayesian acceptance sampling for one lot
accept_bayesian_single.summary: Plan for Bayes-factor evidence and update beliefs from a lot's inspection counts.
accept_bayesian_single.why: You want explicit prior-to-posterior learning about the nonconforming proportion, evidence relative to RQL, and predictions for the remaining lot. This route requires the Acceptance Sampling beta with Bayesian Sampling available.

availability.note: Executed in JASP 0.99.0.0 with an isolated repaired build from hrgodmann/jaspAcceptanceSampling, branch revision/mixture-state-space-model. Activate this exact revision before recomputation; the bundled release and a version label alone are insufficient.

setup.title: Choose quality thresholds and a prior
setup.text: In 1. Planning, enter AQL and RQL. Under Prior Distribution (Beta), choose Impartial (Around the RQL), Uniform, Custom, or Impartial (Three-region). Custom α and β here are Beta shape parameters; they are not producer's and consumer's error risks.

setup.title: Separate evidence from the selected target
setup.text: For this inference-focused preview use Uniform prior, AQL .05, RQL .15, maximum planning n=40 and minimum BF=30. Planning tables are outside the clip. A Bayes-factor evidence label does not automatically prescribe acceptance.

setup.title: Update using inspected items
setup.text: In 2. Inference, select Use data to create posterior distribution. Enter Sample size (n), Observed number of defects (d), and Lot size (N). Select Inference decision table, Posterior plot, and Posterior predictive distribution plot. Counts are typed directly; no CSV assignment is needed.

setup.title: Colleague preview — 7 November 2026
setup.text: Inference preview requires Henrik’s repaired development build at revision 9d08972b6b10b8d04b9650ecce4b1560f811b629, branch revision/mixture-state-space-model, not the bundled release. Uniform prior with n=30, d=0, N=100 gives Beta(1,31). BF for theta < .15 versus theta ≥ .15 is 867.99035; evidence and the selected target 30 are separate. This is not an automatic acceptance recommendation. Predictive total has support 0–70, mean 2.1875, P(D=0)=.3069307 and P(D≤5)=.8965424.

checks: The Beta-Binomial model counts nonconforming items: use 0 ≤ d ≤ n ≤ N. Do not enter multiple flaws per item as d.
With prior Beta(a,b), the posterior is Beta(a+d,b+n−d). The prediction for total lot defects includes those already observed and uncertainty about the uninspected items.
A Bayes-factor threshold is an evidence requirement, not the α/β protection of a classical plan. Report prior choices and check sensitivity.
The standard planning target is below versus above RQL; AQL influences region summaries and some prior specifications. Read the selected hypothesis definitions.

Inference preview requires Henrik’s repaired development build at revision 9d08972b6b10b8d04b9650ecce4b1560f811b629, branch revision/mixture-state-space-model, not the bundled release. Uniform prior with n=30, d=0, N=100 gives Beta(1,31). BF for theta < .15 versus theta ≥ .15 is 867.99035; evidence and the selected target 30 are separate. This is not an automatic acceptance recommendation. Predictive total has support 0–70, mean 2.1875, P(D=0)=.3069307 and P(D≤5)=.8965424.
report: Module beta version, AQL/RQL, prior, planning limit and Bayes-factor target.
n, d, N, posterior summary, Bayes-factor direction, predictive lot-quality probabilities, and decision policy.

example.title: Learn from a sample with no nonconforming seals
example.story: A synthetic example illustrates that observing zero nonconforming items still leaves uncertainty about the rest of the lot.
instructions: Set AQL=.05, RQL=.15, Uniform prior, maximum planning n=40, minimum BF=30.
Enable inference with n=30, d=0, N=100; show posterior and posterior predictive plots.
Check Beta(1,31), Bayes-factor evidence and the selected target separately. Do not convert an evidence label into an acceptance recommendation.

accept_bayesian_sequence.title: Bayesian acceptance sampling across lots
accept_bayesian_sequence.summary: Explore defect-rate changes and predictive uncertainty for the latest lot.
accept_bayesian_sequence.why: Twelve related chronological lots illustrate a changing defect rate under the pinned repaired development model. This preview focuses on retrospective smoothing and latest-lot prediction.

availability.note: Executed in JASP 0.99.0.0 with an isolated repaired build from hrgodmann/jaspAcceptanceSampling, branch revision/mixture-state-space-model. Activate this exact revision before recomputation; the bundled release and a version label alone are insufficient.

setup.title: Assign the chronological data
setup.text: Assign Nonconforming, Tested, LotSize and LotOrder to Defect Count, Sample Size, Lot Size and Lot Number. Leave Covariates empty; one row per unique numeric lot.

setup.title: Specify the model
setup.text: Use initial Beta(1,1) and half-normal baseline innovation scale 1. The repaired model has symmetric mixture innovations; the old post-fit jump correction instruction is obsolete.

setup.title: Inspect diagnostics before interpretation
setup.text: Use three chains, 2000 warmup, 5000 retained draws per chain, thin 1, seed 1, Adapt Delta .99 and maximum treedepth 15. Select MCMC Diagnostics → Print Diagnostics. Inspect divergences, treedepth, rank-normalized R-hat, bulk/tail ESS and per-chain E-BFMI.

setup.title: Colleague preview — 7 November 2026
setup.text: Repaired-build preview at revision 9d08972b6b10b8d04b9650ecce4b1560f811b629 uses all 12 chronological lots with no predictors. Three chains, 2000 warmup, 5000 retained draws per chain, thin 1, seed 1; Adapt Delta .99 resolves one rehearsal divergence at .97. Zero divergences/treedepth hits, maximum rank-normalized R-hat 1.001, minimum bulk/tail ESS 5597/4285, E-BFMI .959/.922/.957. The trajectory is retrospective smoothing, with latest rate about 7.81% and 95% interval [4.38%,12.70%]. Prediction is 9 + Binomial(900,theta), support 9–909; the grouped central-range plot is not the full support. No acceptance-policy claim or prior-sensitivity validation is made.

columns.name: LotOrder
columns.description: Numeric chronological lot order; assign to Lot Number.

columns.name: Nonconforming
columns.description: Integer number of nonconforming sampled items, not separate flaw events; assign to Defect Count.

columns.name: Tested
columns.description: Integer number inspected in that lot; assign to Sample Size (tested items).

columns.name: LotSize
columns.description: Integer total number of items in that lot; assign to Lot Size (total items).

checks: For each row require 0 ≤ Nonconforming ≤ Tested ≤ LotSize; use positive sample and lot sizes. Keep chronological order and explain missing lots or large gaps.
The model shares information across related lots; unrelated suppliers or abrupt process changes need deliberate modelling choices.
The state-space output summarizes the latest lot, with a trajectory over the sequence. It is not a classical control chart or proof of stability.

Repaired-build preview at revision 9d08972b6b10b8d04b9650ecce4b1560f811b629 uses all 12 chronological lots with no predictors. Three chains, 2000 warmup, 5000 retained draws per chain, thin 1, seed 1; Adapt Delta .99 resolves one rehearsal divergence at .97. Zero divergences/treedepth hits, maximum rank-normalized R-hat 1.001, minimum bulk/tail ESS 5597/4285, E-BFMI .959/.922/.957. The trajectory is retrospective smoothing, with latest rate about 7.81% and 95% interval [4.38%,12.70%]. Prediction is 9 + Binomial(900,theta), support 9–909; the grouped central-range plot is not the full support. No acceptance-policy claim or prior-sensitivity validation is made.

All rows must satisfy 0 ≤ defects ≤ inspected ≤ lot size. Numeric lot order determines ordering, not transition spacing. Earlier rates use later observations; these are smoothed estimates. Prior sensitivity and predictive calibration remain outside this preview.
report: Exact development revision, chronological data, no-predictor model, priors and sampler settings.
Trajectory, latest-lot predictive support and uncertainty, computational diagnostics and limits; do not claim a validated acceptance policy.

example.title: Inspect a sequence of component lots
example.story: Twelve synthetic ordered lots have 100 inspected components each. Nonconforming counts rise in the final lots to illustrate changing quality.
instructions: Assign the four original columns to matching roles; leave Covariates empty.
Use the model and MCMC settings above, including Adapt Delta .99. Print the complete diagnostic report before interpreting plots.
Retain AQL .05/RQL .10 and illustrative thresholds .10/.05 only as context. Focus on the smoothed trajectory and latest-lot prediction; no automatic policy is taught.
